findings.claim: R8 asks for D_1 on all local operators; what is computed is only the two-body log kernel (4 lc^natural). The composite two-body kernel C^(2)_Delta and the one-body C^(1)_Delta (A_V, lambda, c) are computed by neither engine, so every D_1 number reported for gauge-invariant families (two_site.json D1_eigenvalues_units, kernels.json D1 'spectrum_at_theta=-1/3_under_P7', P5 eig(D_1) = -8 E_H u) is conditional on the untested prediction P7. On the bilinears the engines take the composite triangle -2u {S^(1)(Delta),O} from Prop c9-triangle; Remark c9-twoeval states that 'this agreement determines both coefficients 8 in the value of the composite triangle', i.e. that input was fixed by consistency, not evaluated. D_1 on the bilinears is therefore an input to R8, not a check of it.
findings.evidence: engine_a/kernels.json D1.two_body: 'C^(2)_Delta ... NOT computed by engine A'; engine_b/NOTES.md 'the composite parts ... are not computed by route B'; compare.json open_issues[0]; manuscript ch09 Rem rem:c9-twoeval last sentence. The referee confirms 4 lc^natural (R7, R9, R10) but has no independent value for C_Delta.
findings.fix: Evaluate C^(2)_Delta (composite cycles through a pair, composite kernel 2(P* v. P* (x) 1)K_0 of Def c9-composite) directly, first for (A_perp, A_perp) without derivatives (this independently reproduces or refutes Prop c9-triangle), then for the twist-two pairs (d^a Z, d^b Z) and (A_n, Z), to test P7. Until then label every D_1 eigenvalue 'conditional on P7, theta = -1/3' and quote spectra as 2 eig lc^natural = gamma.
findings.two_component: D_1 = 4 lc^natural - {F'_Delta,-} + C_Delta; on (A_ij, A_kl) only the term u[8 A_kl A_ij - 2 eps_ijkl A^mn A_mn] (= 4 x two-site log kernel) is computed.

findings.claim: Lemma lem:tl-colour labels the outputs opposite to Def def:tl-cycle and to both engines. With Y_1 at the vertex nearest X_a (the numbering of Def tl-cycle), the chain gives the colour element sum t_gamma (x) ad_{Y_k}...ad_{Y_1} t^gamma, and the planar replacement is Y_1...Y_k. The Lemma writes w = ad_{Y_1}...ad_{Y_r} and 'replaced by Y_r...Y_1' without saying which Y is nearest X_a. Combining the Lemma's order with the Def tl-cycle numbering swaps the swap and identity terms of the planar density: u[2P - K] becomes u[2 - K], which gives lc^natural = 0 on every su(2) state and contradicts the Heisenberg spectrum.
findings.evidence: Referee derivation of the colour contraction along the chain (ref_core.py docstring) and t_colour.py (explicit gl(N) matrices): the leading term is +N tr(M1 Y_1 Y_2) with Y_1 nearest X_a. The engines use this reading (kernels.json meta 'tr(... Y_1 ... Y_r ...)'), and the su(2) and twist-two spectra (R7, R9) confirm it.
findings.fix: In Lemma lem:tl-colour (i) state 'Y_r adjacent to X_a, Y_1 adjacent to X_b' or rewrite (i)-(iii) with w = ad_{Y_r}...ad_{Y_1} (Y_1 nearest X_a) and 'replaced by Y_1...Y_r'.

findings.claim: Table tab:tl-A lists the self-contraction (empty leg set) in the eps^{-1} column of (lambda_+, lambda_-) and (c, A*|_V) at W_0 = 3. Lemma lem:tl-k0 in the same document makes K^(0) a single power eps^{-W/2}, which vanishes when W is odd, so this entry is identically zero.
findings.evidence: compare.json census_check.predicted_but_zero (A_W0 and B_W0: lamP|lamM and c|AsV '(none) eps^-1'); the referee's kernel_k0 returns no singular part for odd W (t_deriv.py k=0 cases agree with the Lemma).
findings.fix: Remove the empty set from the eps^{-1} column of those two rows (keep A|_V), or add a footnote that the census lists slot-allowed topologies and that this one vanishes by Lemma lem:tl-k0.

findings.claim: Engine B fixed the overall sign of the odd-pair kernels empirically, by requiring W1 to hold (NOTES.md: the naive left-derivative argument gave -1, with +1 they hold). In engine B the W1 gates for (A_perp, c) and (A_V, c) are therefore not independent tests. The sign is nevertheless correct: the referee's explicit Koszul reordering of <X_a X_b V_1 ... V_k> gives the same odd-pair kernels as engines A and B (R3), and W1 and W2 hold with them (R11, R12).
findings.evidence: engine_b/NOTES.md 'Definition computed'; t_ghost.py: A_V|c, A_perp|c, A_V|A*_V, A_perp|A*_V all agree, 0 mismatches; t_ward1.py K(A_mu,c)|_c = i r_mu; t_ward2b.py.
findings.fix: Record in engine B the derivation of the sign: K(X_a,X_b) = hbar Sing <X_a X_b>_e with P^{phi psi} the two-point function, first factor first, and Koszul reordering. No number changes.

findings.claim: In two_site.json the 'D1_eigenvalues_units' strings omit u (already compare F-3). They also append '- (1/3+theta) v.', which is the classical dilatation operator and not a number, so the strings mix an operator with eigenvalues. The engine A notes give 'one-body parts in units' A_V -22/3, lambda -47/3, c -8/3; these leave out the nonlocal C^(1)_Delta, and only the sum C^(1)+C^(2) is local.
findings.evidence: engine_b/two_site.json twist_two['8'].D1_eigenvalues_units = ['-3044/35 - (1/3+theta) v.', ...]; engine_a/kernels.json D1.one_body_units. Arithmetic checked: -4 n_F - {F'_Delta,-} gives -8+2/3 = -22/3, -16+1/3 = -47/3, -4+4/3 = -8/3, and with Pi_Delta|perp the A_perp value -8 + (5/3 - theta) v.
findings.fix: Report eigenvalues as numbers times u (conditional on P7, N1) and keep the classical part separate. Label the A_V, lambda, c one-body numbers 'without C^(1)_Delta (nonlocal)'.

findings.claim: The Ward identity W2 (Cor cor:tl-ward) was run by neither engine nor the comparator. The referee checked two instances, both pass: tr(zeta A_I A_J) at outputs (A_perp, A_perp, c), and tr(zeta A_mu A_I) at outputs (c, A_perp) with one derivative, where w + x = (i/2) q1_mu delta_IK holds with w = 3i q1_mu/2 and x = -i q1_mu. W2 for fermion, ghost and antifield pairs remains untested.
findings.fix: Add W2 gates in both engines for (lambda_+, lambda_-), (c, A*_V) and (A_V, A_V) with derivatives, at the lowest number of output fields.

findings.claim: The two-engine agreement covers only W <= W_0 + 2; engine B has no tables above that. Higher W and k >= 3 rest on engine A alone. The referee confirms engine A there exactly: bosonic letters at W = 5, 6 (log, eps^-1, eps^-2), fermion pairs with three derivatives (W = 6), A|lambda at W = 11/2, and k = 3 chains, with 0 mismatches.
findings.fix: Quote the coverage explicitly in the compare report: two engines up to W_0+2, engine A plus referee beyond.
